fundamental.thesis: Canara HSBC Life Insurance (CANHLIFE) is a bancassurance-focused life insurer distributed primarily through the Canara Bank and PNB branch networks, giving it a structural reach advantage over standalone agency-model peers; however, for a life insurer the correct valuation yardstick is P/EV (Price-to-Embedded Value), not P/E, and P/EV data is absent from this pack. Revenue growth has been strong at +25% YoY in FY26 (peaking at +31.6% at 9M before settling), but PAT has grown only +8.5% as PAT margin contracted from 1.6% (H1 FY26) to 1.3% (FY26 full year), meaning topline momentum is not converting to bottom-line expansion — a concerning quality signal; crucially, H1 FY27 results were filed on 9-Oct-2026 but remain unextracted, leaving the current trajectory blind. As the best available proxy, P/B at 8.29× against a TTM ROE of only 8.1% is clearly expensive (P/B < 1.5 + ROE > 12% = cheap; this is the inverse), and broad-market peer rank at P94 on trailing P/E (107×, +205% vs median 35×) and P98 on forward P/E confirm top-decile expensiveness with no margin of safety. The single biggest risk is that thin, contracting PAT margins (1.3%) combined with a ₹287.5 cr NCD issuance signalling capital needs leave the earnings base fragile — any claims spike, cost overrun, or distribution slowdown would disproportionately impair an already leverage-heavy, low-ROE profile in a RISK_OFF macro regime where Financials are macro-underweight.

Revenue growth has slowed from +30.7% in FY26 to +19.0%, then +15.9%, and now +6.6% YoY in Q2FY27 (₹10,294 cr). PAT fell 34.0% YoY to ₹523 cr (from ₹793 cr), the third straight quarter of falling profit. PAT margin is 5.1%, against 6.0% for FY26. Earnings are also turning into cash poorly: H1 cash from operations was only ₹54 cr against ₹1,220 cr of pre-tax profit, as working capital absorbed the cash. I used EV/EBITDA as the main measure because this is a capital-intensive, subsidy-linked business. At 17.3x it sits almost exactly at the Materials peer median of 17.9x (P47). Trailing P/E is 31.6x, 15% below the peer median of 37.3x but above the 12–22x generic Materials range, and that peer set is skewed upward by paint companies. The main risk is that the expected recovery doesn't arrive: analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by 10.7% over 90 days while 8 of 9 still rate it a buy. That pattern often comes before a re-rating downward, and rising crude and imported ammonia/sulphur costs (about 80% import-dependent) could squeeze margins further.

That recovery comes off a weak, weather-hit base, though. Implied Q2 PAT was only about ₹47 cr, and that figure includes a ₹63 cr Sidra guarantee write-back and ₹15 cr of prior-period PLI incentive, so the underlying Q2 profit was thin. EMP project revenue also fell 21.2%. On valuation I used P/E and EV/EBITDA against peers, as the sector card suggests for durables. The trailing P/E of 86x is 116% above the sector median of 39.7x (P94), and EV/EBITDA of 47.8x sits at P89. The forward P/E of 36x already prices in a full earnings recovery, so the stock grades expensive even though it trades near its 52-week low. The biggest risk is that the recovery story keeps losing steam: analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by 7.7% over 90 days, operating cash flow was negative in H1, and commodity and currency pressure on margins could trigger a de-rating even if volumes stay strong.

fundamental.thesis: Aarti Industries is a mid-cap Indian specialty chemicals maker (benzene-based intermediates for agrochem, pharma and polymers), a cyclical business that stands to gain from China+1 sourcing shifts. The revenue figures in the filings disagree with each other (the H1 total of ₹6,065 cr does not match the two quarters added together), so the reported +41% to +60% revenue growth rates are not reliable; the PAT figures do add up. Using EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for chemical cyclicals, the stock trades at 19.4x, well above the sector card's mid-cycle norm of 5–8x, and 42x trailing P/E is above the 12–22x Materials range; ROE is only 7.2% against 2.95x book, and the price sits at 80% of its 52-week range, so it looks expensive even though the forward P/E of 24x and sell-side upgrades (+5.2% over 30 days) already assume strong earnings growth.

fundamental.thesis: Gujarat Fluorochemicals is a major Indian maker of fluoropolymers and fluorochemicals; its chemicals arm brings in about 98% of revenue, and it is also building a battery-materials (EV) business that is still at an early stage. Growth has picked up sharply. Revenue growth went from -1.1% in Q3FY26 to +12% in Q4FY26, +24% in Q1FY27 (₹1,588 cr) and +34.4% for H1FY27 (₹3,348 cr). That implies a Q2FY27 of about ₹1,760 cr, up roughly 45% YoY, with PAT of about ₹240 cr (about 13.6% margin). EBITDA margin rose from 22.5% to about 27%, the chemicals segment earned a 27.6% margin, and cash from operations was 1.61x PAT. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card sets for capital-intensive chemicals. At 42.2x it is far above the card's 5–8x mid-cycle range and in the 84th percentile of the broad market. Trailing P/E is 85.3x and forward P/E 43.5x, the stock sits at 91.5% of its 52-week range, and the mean analyst target is only about 1.7% above the price, so it is expensive even allowing for a premium for fluoropolymer quality. The biggest risk is the gap between price and estimates: analysts have cut forecasts (FY EPS -2.5%, next-FY -5.4%) while ratings stay bullish, which often comes before a de-rating. On top of that, the planned ₹6,000 cr battery-materials capex is pushing free cash flow negative (₹-103 cr in H1) while that segment is still losing money (₹-92 cr in H1).

fundamental.thesis: UPL is India's largest global agrochemical company, operating crop protection (UPL Corp), seeds (Advanta), and post-harvest segments across 130+ countries — a capital-intensive, leveraged cyclical recovering from a multi-year agrochem destocking cycle. Revenue has accelerated from a trough of +2% YoY in Q1FY26 to +10% YoY in Q1FY27 (₹10,181 cr consolidated); EBITDA grew 15% YoY to ₹1,500 cr with 180 bps contribution-margin expansion, and Q1FY27 PATMI was management's stated strongest in three years — a clear directional improvement from the -₹88 cr loss in Q1FY26, supported by broad-based platform growth (Advanta +26%, SUPERFORM +14%, UPL Corp +7%). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per sector card guidance), UPL at 7.86× sits at P6 vs. 473 broad-market peers (67% discount to the 23.3× median) and at the mid-cycle floor for specialty chemicals (5–8× range); forward P/E of 12.65× is 46% below trailing 27.34×, signalling substantial earnings recovery priced in — the stock grades cheap on the appropriate metric. The primary risk is the combination of very high financial leverage (D/E flagged as extreme), NWC deteriorating sharply to 110 days (+24 days YoY from inventory build and FX translation), and persistent China-led price competition in agrochemicals — all amplified by rising crude input costs, INR weakness expanding USD-denominated debt service costs, and an ongoing RISK_OFF macro regime with FII net selling.

fundamental.thesis: Cohance Lifesciences is an Indian CDMO/API platform (formerly Suven Pharmaceuticals) serving global pharma innovators across Pharma CDMO, API+, Sapala nucleic-acid specialty chemicals, and Formulations — a niche franchise currently navigating a sharp operational trough driven by post-merger NJ Bio consolidation, Pharma CDMO order phasing, and Specialty Chemicals destocking. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue declined 23.1% YoY to ₹422 cr (decelerating sharply from +12.5% in Q1FY26 and extending the -13.1% full-year FY26 decline), with Pharma CDMO down 38.7% YoY, NJ Bio contributing an EBITDA loss of ₹328 mn, and PAT swinging to ₹-45 cr (-176% YoY); EBITDA margins imploded 2,220bps to 2.2%, though gross margins held at 71.5% and FCF remained a healthy ₹106 cr — indicating the trough is volume/timing-driven rather than structural margin destruction, and management has guided Q1FY27 as the floor with H2FY27 YoY recovery. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick per sector card guidance for a capital-intensive CDMO, the stock trades at 39.3× (P81 vs broad-market peers, 68% premium to median 23.3×), expensive on any normalised basis; trailing P/E of 88.6× (P91, distorted by the trough PAT) and forward P/E of 38.9× still sit well above sector Pharma medians of 28–40×, while sell-side FY EPS estimates have been cut 25.5% in the last 30 days — suggesting the recovery the market is paying for is actively being revised downward. The biggest risk is binary: an active FDA Warning Letter at the Nacharam FDF facility, if not resolved swiftly, could trigger customer qualification audits across the CDMO business precisely when the recovery pipeline depends on securing and delivering new orders against a backdrop of dangerously high Debt/Equity of 9.93.

fundamental.thesis: Zee Entertainment is India's second-largest broadcast media group (~50 TV channels plus the ZEE5 OTT platform), structurally pressured by the secular migration to streaming and left exposed after the Jiostar/Sony merger collapsed; it now carries substantial governance and legal overhangs that suppress any re-rating. FY26 annual revenue declined 1.9% YoY to ₹7,567 Cr while PAT collapsed 82.8% to ₹120 Cr, compressing PAT margin to 1.6% and EBITDA margin to a catastrophic 2.6% (from 13.4% in FY25) — the multi-quarter trajectory shows revenue decelerating and margins contracting across every available period with no stabilisation evident in filings. Forward P/E of 13.42× (P19 vs broad-market peers, -42% below median) and P/B of 0.9× (P2 vs peers, -80% below median) both screen as unambiguously cheap; EV/EBITDA of 23× looks deceptively at median but is computed on severely depressed EBITDA — on normalised 12-13% margins the implied EV/EBITDA would be sub-5×, confirming franchise-level cheapness if operational recovery is achievable. The single largest risk to the recovery thesis is the IDBI Bank insolvency petition (filed September 2025) seeking NCLT-admitted CIRP initiation, which if granted would be existential for the business regardless of underlying brand and content-IP value.

Rainbow Children's Medicare runs a chain of 26 hospitals focused on children's and women's care (65% paediatrics, 30% women's care). Revenue growth has picked up for three quarters in a row, from +6.5% to +11.9% to +12.4% and now +23.2% YoY in Q2FY27 (₹548 cr), but profit grew only +10.9% to ₹84 cr. That is because PAT margin slipped from 17.0% to 15.3% and EBITDA margin from 33.5% to 31.0%, as 5 new hospitals with only 27.4% occupancy and a -16% EBITDA margin weigh on group profit. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the right measure for a hospital business with heavy capital needs: at 26.1x it is only about 12% above the broad-market median (P59), and the forward P/E of 36.5x against a trailing 51.3x shows earnings growth is expected, so the stock looks fair, not cheap. The peer comparison is a broad-market fallback with no hospital peers in the set, and live data looks partly unreliable (24% dividend yield, D/E printed as 53.56), so the grade is only moderately confident. The main risk to the thesis is that profit lags revenue for longer than expected while new beds ramp up: analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by 4% over 90 days even though all 14 still rate it a buy, a common pattern before a stock re-rates lower.

fundamental.thesis: Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands is a mid-cap branded apparel company that owns Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly and Peter England, plus a smaller emerging-brands portfolio. It sells through 3,434 stores, 40,500 multi-brand outlets, 6,800 shop-in-shops, e-commerce and wholesale. In Q2FY27, revenue grew 11.0% YoY to Rs 2,266 cr, up from +3.7% in Q2FY26 and +9.6% in Q3FY26, the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth. PAT rose 126% to Rs 53 cr, but the PAT margin is still thin at 2.3%. EBITDA margin widened 60 bps to 17.2% and same-store (LTL) retail sales grew 5.3%, the 8th positive quarter in a row, though that is slower than before. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a store-heavy retailer, the stock trades at 15.9x versus a broad-market median of 23.3x (P28), and the forward P/E of 27x is far below the sector card's 60-100x range. The trailing P/E of 58x looks expensive only because current profits are low. I grade valuation fair, and the price sitting near its 52-week low gives a reasonable entry point. The main risk is profitability: net profit is only about 2% of revenue, and debt plus lease liabilities are high, so a weak festive season or slower same-store sales could wipe out much of the profit gain.

fundamental.thesis: Brainbees (FirstCry) is India's largest multi-channel retailer for baby and kids products, with GlobalBees brand roll-ups, an international arm and preschools on the side. It is still not reliably profitable. In Q1FY27 consolidated revenue grew about 13% YoY, which management calls the best in 5 years, and India multi-channel grew 18% with same-store sales growth of 15%. Growth has been uneven rather than accelerating: +18.2% in FY25, then +11.4%, then +13.0%. Profitability is getting worse: adjusted EBITDA was flat YoY, India multi-channel EBITDA margin fell 290 bps, and the gross margin is still 260 bps short of where it was. The data for profit is unreliable: the trend table shows PAT of ₹51 cr (+34%), while yfinance shows a loss of ₹31 cr on revenue of ₹1,337 cr, and the filings index says its latest extracted results are from H1 FY26, so I am not relying on any PAT figure. The sector card says to judge loss-making platforms like this one on EV/sales, growth and unit economics, not P/E. On that basis the stock is fair rather than cheap: price/sales of 1.24x and P/B of 2.18x are low for a platform, but EV/EBITDA of 159x (most expensive in its peer set) and a forward P/E of 49x mean you are paying for a margin recovery that hasn't happened yet. The stock sits near its 52-week low, but analysts' FY estimates have been cut 15–18% over 90 days. The biggest risk is that Q2 results on 14 Nov show the promised gross-margin recovery not arriving, as quick-commerce and pharmacy competitors keep pressuring diapers (about 15% of GMV).

fundamental.thesis: Gabriel India is a domestic auto-component maker focused on shock absorbers and suspension. It leads in commercial vehicles (about 88% market share) and electric two-wheelers (about 57%), and about 40% of revenue comes from the replacement/aftermarket business. H1 FY27 revenue grew 20.8% YoY to Rs 2,673 cr, speeding up from +15.5% in Q1 FY27 and +14.8% for FY26. That leaves an implied Q2 of about Rs 1,247 cr. Profits are not keeping up: PBT grew only about 10% YoY, Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 8.7% against 9.6% in FY26, and the restatement after the demerger plus the new stakes in HL Mando Anand and HL Klemove make the growth partly inorganic and harder to compare year on year. Valuation is expensive however you measure it. The trailing P/E of 65x is far above the 18-28x auto band. EV/EBITDA of 36.9x (the main yardstick here, since the business is shifting toward a capital- and acquisition-heavy holding structure) and P/B of 12x sit in the top quartile of the broad market (P77 and P88). The forward P/E of 31.8x and recent FY EPS upgrades (+6.2% over 30 days) already assume strong earnings growth, while next-year estimates are edging down (-1.2% over 30 days). The biggest risk is that the deals take net debt from about Rs 2 cr to Rs 1,125 cr while operating cash flow falls 36% YoY, so any slip in integration or margins hits a stock priced for perfection.

fundamental.thesis: Patanjali Foods is India's largest edible oils company (formerly Ruchi Soya), with a fast-growing FMCG overlay spanning biscuits, nutrition, and home/personal care under the Patanjali brand — but edible oils still account for roughly 70%+ of revenues, making this a commodity-FMCG hybrid rather than a pure compounder, and that matters critically for how to frame the valuation. Q1FY27 delivered record revenue of ₹11,337 cr (+29.3% YoY, accelerating from +20.9% in Q2FY26) and PAT of ₹336 cr (+86.1% YoY), but underlying quality is deteriorating: gross margin compressed from 15.26% (Q2FY26) to 13.42% (Q1FY27), EBITDA margin fell from 6.2% to 4.8%, and PAT margin contracted to 3.0% — a persistent multi-quarter contraction signal that runs counter to the top-line acceleration. At trailing P/E 25.43×, the stock screens cheap versus the FMCG sector benchmark of 40–60×, but the discount is structurally warranted by the commodity-heavy business mix; EV/EBITDA of 25× (P55 vs broad-market peers) and P/E peer rank of P32 both point to fair value rather than genuine mispricing, and the sector card's own caution — 'cheap FMCG usually means a structural problem' — applies directly here. The overriding risk is extreme balance sheet leverage (D/E 21.3×) combined with negative FCF (CFO/PAT −1.13× in Q2FY26) — at a 5.29% US 10Y yield and with PAT margins at 3%, any commodity cost spike or interest burden increase could rapidly destroy earnings entirely.

Ramkrishna Forgings makes forged and machined parts, mainly for commercial vehicles, rail and global auto platforms, and has subsidiaries in the USA and Mexico. In H1 FY27 revenue grew 36.3% YoY to ₹2,621 cr and PAT rose to ₹117 cr from ₹2 cr, with EBITDA margin up from 14.6% to 18.1%. Revenue growth has improved quarter by quarter, from -4.5% (H1 FY26) to +19.8% (Q1 FY27) to +36.3% (H1 FY27), but much of that comes off a weak base hit by a ₹42 cr provision on bad receivables, and the yfinance quarterly figures (₹734 cr in Q2) do not match the filing-based table. Because this is a capital-intensive business, I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA: 20.0x is P42 against the market and about 14% below the median, and a forward P/E of 27.7x sits at the top of the 18-28x auto-ancillary range. The 148x trailing P/E is inflated by the depressed base, so overall valuation looks fair, and with the price at the consensus target (₹697) there is little room left. The biggest weakness is cash: operating cash flow was only ₹41.5 cr in H1 (0.35x PAT) against ₹390 cr of capex, so free cash flow was -₹349 cr, inventory is building and finance costs take 4.5% of revenue. Return on equity is weak at 2.3%.

fundamental.thesis: Cyient is a mid-cap engineering-services firm with three businesses: design and engineering services (DET, about 74% of revenue), electronics contract manufacturing (DLM), and a loss-making semiconductor unit, and it recently bought TAO Digital for about ₹2,156 cr. H1 FY27 revenue grew 23.4% YoY to ₹4,311 cr, but that growth is largely acquisition-driven, and PAT fell 19.7% YoY to ₹241 cr, so the PAT margin dropped from 8.6% to 5.6%. Profit has now fallen in every reported period (-24.9% in Q3FY26, -32.3% in Q1FY27, -19.7% in H1FY27), and the semiconductor unit lost ₹58 cr at a -16.5% margin. On valuation, I used P/E and EV/EBITDA together, and the stock looks fair rather than cheap: trailing P/E of 22.6x sits at the bottom of the 22–30x IT range, and EV/EBITDA of 11.4x ranks P16 against the broad market, but ROE is only 7.8%. The low 11.9x forward P/E rests on analyst estimates that were cut 18% over the last 90 days, so it should not be trusted yet. The biggest risk is that semiconductor losses and integrating TAO keep eating into the steady DET profits, and the data has gaps: the yfinance Q2 revenue of ₹1,498 cr conflicts with the filings, Q1FY27 shows two different growth rates, and the reported debt/equity and dividend-yield figures look like data errors.

Intellect Design Arena is a mid-cap banking and insurance software maker. It sells licences, platform subscriptions and maintenance (AMC) to more than 500 financial institutions in 62 countries. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹855 cr, up 13.0% YoY, and growth has slowed over the trend window from +36.2% (Q2 FY26) to +20.6% (Q1FY27) to +13.0%. PAT was ₹104 cr, up only 1.8% YoY, and the PAT margin fell to 12.2% from 13.5% a year ago. EBITDA margin was 23.2% vs 24.3% a year ago, while LTM EBITDA margin fell about 344 bps to 22.4%, and LTM PBT is down 6.2%; management puts over ₹100 cr of that on AI investment. On the main IT yardstick, trailing P/E is 31.2×, just above the 22–30× sector range. The forward P/E of 18.4× and EV/EBITDA of 17.0× sit well below the broad-market median (P31–P43), so I grade it fair rather than cheap. The forward P/E leans on earnings growth that analysts are now cutting: FY EPS estimates are down about 10% and next-year estimates about 13% over 30–90 days. The biggest risk is that the heavy AI spending (the MSOCK platform) keeps squeezing margins while revenue growth keeps slowing, so revenue growth stops turning into profit growth.

fundamental.thesis: HINDPETRO is a state-run oil marketing and refining company whose earnings depend mainly on the gap between crude costs and government-influenced retail fuel and LPG prices. Q2FY27 revenue was about ₹1,39,213 cr (H1 ₹2,84,339 cr minus Q1 ₹1,45,126 cr), up roughly 26% YoY from ₹1,10,323 cr, but this growth comes from higher prices rather than profit: Q2 PAT recovered to ₹3,625 cr (2.6% margin, partly helped by ₹3,960 cr of H1 LPG compensation) after a Q1 loss of ₹12,265 cr, leaving H1 at a ₹8,639 cr loss and H1 EBITDA margin at -1.9% versus about 6.7% a year earlier. Using P/E plus dividend yield and EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card sets for OMCs, the headline 4.7x trailing P/E and 4.2x EV/EBITDA look like the cheapest in the market, but they are stale: they reflect FY26 PAT of ₹18,047 cr, while actual trailing-four-quarter PAT is only about ₹1,200 cr (roughly 70x). The 7.3x forward P/E is therefore better read as policy-priced and fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is crude above $100 with a weakening rupee: marketing losses could return while the balance sheet is already stretched, with short-term borrowings up to ₹35,933 cr, a current ratio of 0.57, negative interest coverage and an ₹18,049 cr unrecognised LPG under-recovery.

fundamental.thesis: Shree Cement is a large Indian cement maker with a growing UAE business and is expanding toward a long-term capacity target of 80 MT. Revenue growth accelerated from +4.0% in Q3FY26 to +23.9% in Q2FY27 (Rs 5,897 cr, on 14% higher consolidated volumes), but PAT fell 15.2% to Rs 263 cr, while EBITDA margin dropped from 23.8% in Q1FY27 to 17.2% and EBITDA per tonne fell 8% YoY to Rs 966, near the low end of the Rs 900-1,100 healthy range. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick, the stock looks expensive at a snapshot 30.4x versus a 17.9x peer median (P80), and its 48.6x trailing P/E is well above the 37.3x peer median and the 12-22x Materials benchmark; however, TTM EBITDA from the filings implies only about 18x EV/EBITDA, so the grade leans more on P/E and is held with moderate confidence despite the stock sitting near its 52-week low (19% of range). The biggest risk is that revenue growth keeps failing to reach profit as fuel costs stay high with crude rising, a concern reflected in FY EPS estimates being cut 14.1% in 30 days despite a mostly bullish rating mix, while the snapshot's 66% dividend yield and 38.15 debt/equity are treated as data errors (the filings show debt/equity of 0.08).

IGL is the main city gas distributor in Delhi NCR, selling CNG to vehicles and piped gas (PNG) to homes and businesses. It is still adding volume: total volumes grew 6.9% YoY to 9.86 MMSCMD in H1 FY27, CNG rose 7.5% and domestic PNG rose 11.5%. Profits, however, have collapsed. H1 FY27 revenue grew 21.4% to ₹10,654 cr, but gas purchase costs jumped 39%, EBITDA margin fell from 12% to 3%, and PAT dropped 71% to ₹211 cr (a 2.0% margin). Q2 alone was much worse: EBITDA was negative ₹31 cr and PAT was about ₹26 cr, down roughly 93% from ₹386 cr a year earlier. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA and P/E, as suits a capital-intensive utility. On those, the stock looks cheap: trailing P/E is 15.4x (inside the 10–18x utilities range), EV/EBITDA is 10.5x and the stock sits around the 12th–15th percentile of the market. But both figures are based on trailing earnings that are falling fast, and analysts have cut current-year EPS estimates by 50–59% in 90 days. So I grade it fair, and the low multiples may be a value trap. The biggest risk is that IGL cannot raise CNG and PNG prices to cover higher gas costs (in a politically sensitive Delhi market, with crude near $91 and rising), so margins stay crushed.

fundamental.thesis: Inventurus Knowledge Solutions (IKS) handles outsourced revenue-cycle management and clinical support work for US doctors and hospitals. It is a fast-growing midcap that sits between IT services and healthcare, and it is not directly exposed to the time-and-materials deflation hurting generic IT services. The latest quarter we have extracted, Q1 FY27, shows revenue of about ₹894 cr, up 20.7% YoY, and PAT of ₹194 cr, up 27.8%, for a 21.7% PAT margin. Growth is steady at around 20–21% but edging down from +21.5%, and PAT margin has slipped from 23.1% to 21.7%; FY26 revenue was ₹3,194 cr (+19.9%) with a 34.2% EBITDA margin. Valuation is fair rather than cheap. We used EV/EBITDA (25.4×) and forward P/E (25.7×) as the yardstick: both are near the broad-market medians (P57/P56), and forward P/E is well below trailing P/E (39.8×), which signals expected earnings growth. On top of that, sell-side estimates have been raised (+9% for FY27 and +18% for next year over 90 days), but P/B is high at 10.4× (P83) and the stock is at 71% of its 52-week range. The biggest open question is the TruBridge acquisition (USD 557M EV, closed July 9, 2026). It is large relative to a ₹29,200 cr company, adds a lower-margin acute-care EHR/RCM business and a lot of goodwill, and has likely raised debt. The Q2 FY27 results that first include TruBridge were filed on 2026-11-05 but are not in our extracted data, so the margin hit and leverage are still unconfirmed.

fundamental.thesis: JSW Steel is a large Indian steelmaker that sold a record 7.46 MT in Q2FY27 (+13% YoY), with auto-sector sales up 36%. Revenue growth accelerated from +9.8% in Q1 to +20.6% (₹54,486 cr), and PAT rose 225.6% to ₹5,359 cr, though the YoY figures use a low, restructured base; PAT margin was flat at about 9.8-9.9%, the 'contracting' signal is distorted by FY26's ₹18,051 cr one-off gain, and EBITDA per tonne fell about 11% QoQ from ₹14,990 to ₹13,329 despite rising 24% YoY. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a steel cyclical, the stock is expensive: the reported 12.6x, or roughly 9x on my estimate using annualised Q2 EBITDA and net debt, is above the 5-8x mid-cycle norm, and the 13.8x trailing P/E and 'cheap vs peers' verdict carry little weight because of the one-off gain and a peer set that includes paint and adhesive companies. The biggest risk is that steel spreads narrow from here, with the stock at 92% of its 52-week range and EBITDA per tonne already falling sequentially, leaving little room for error.

NTPC is India's largest power generator. Most of its earnings come from a regulated return (about 15.5% ROE) on the plants it has commissioned, with a fast-growing solar and renewables arm on top. H1 FY27 headline revenue was ₹100,262 cr, up 19.9% from ₹83,660 cr a year ago, but the company's core capacity-plus-energy billing grew a more modest 9.65%. Within that, capacity charges rose 6.7% to ₹35,909 cr, energy charges rose 11.6% to ₹55,845 cr and solar revenue rose 64.9% to ₹2,456 cr. Revenue growth has turned up from about -1.5% to -3% in FY26 to +7.0% in Q1 FY27 (PAT ₹6,896 cr, +12.9%, 13.6% margin), though H1 PAT was not extracted. For a capital-intensive utility I graded valuation mainly on EV/EBITDA, backed by P/B with ROE. On that basis it looks cheap against peers: EV/EBITDA is 8.4x against a peer median of 11.6x (cheapest in the peer group) and trailing P/E is 11.9x against 14.7x. P/B is 1.7x with ROE of 13.7%. It is only fair against the static 10–18x utilities P/E band. The forward P/E (12.8x) is above the trailing P/E, and this year's EPS estimates were trimmed 0.9% in the last 30 days, so near-term earnings look roughly flat. The main risk is earnings quality: CERC 2024 tariff orders are still pending, so bills are provisional and later adjusted (₹2,825 cr energy adjustment in H1), and large regulatory-deferral and deferred-tax swings make reported PAT hard to compare across periods.

The biggest risk is that 99% of the book is floating-rate, so it reprices down quickly in an easing cycle, and with growth this thin, earnings depend on low credit costs holding.

fundamental.thesis: Laurus Labs is a vertically integrated API and CDMO business with a dominant ARV generics franchise (41% of FY26 revenue) and a rapidly scaling CDMO segment (30%+ of FY26 revenue, targeting 50% by FY30) supported by 8,200 kl reactor capacity, 110 active CDMO pipeline projects, and zero critical audit findings across 132 inspections — a credible China+1 CDMO beneficiary. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive CDMO/API model, the stock trades at 52.5x vs a sector median of 21.4x — a 145% premium — and ranks P100 (most expensive) across trailing P/E (96.6x), forward P/E (67.2x), P/B (19.8x), and EV/EBITDA in its 14-stock peer group, with the stock at 99.1% of its 52-week range: unambiguously expensive even granting a deserved CDMO re-rating premium. A ₹3,000 cr capex programme (nearly 3× the prior ₹1,000 cr guidance) must convert to contracted CDMO revenue without material slippage while the stock prices in near-flawless execution, with a pending US generics tariff review and inherent CDMO quarter-to-quarter lumpiness creating headline risk at this multiple.

That makes it fair, not cheap, despite 18 of 18 analysts rating it buy and FY-EPS estimates raised 8.7% over 90 days. The main risks are a mid-cap luxury-discretionary stock in a RISK_OFF market with rising crude, and the live price data contradicting itself: the 52-week range of ₹382–474 conflicts with the consensus target of ₹702 implying +16.9% upside, and yfinance Q1 revenue of ₹114 cr does not match the PDF figure of ₹352 cr.

Honasa Consumer is a digital-first personal-care company in FMCG, with brands including Mamaearth, The Derma Co (now above ₹1,000cr ARR) and the recently acquired BTM male-grooming business; it is scaling its offline and quick-commerce channels against legacy FMCG players. The latest quarter we have extracted is Q1FY27: revenue was ₹880cr, up 32.0% YoY, with 30.5% volume growth, and PAT was ₹90cr at a 10.2% margin. Growth has sped up from +11.6% (H1FY26) to +15.7% (FY26) to +32%, and PAT margin has risen from 7.1% to 10.2%. Some of that growth comes from the BTM acquisition, and volume growth above 10% should be treated with scepticism. Valuation is graded on P/E plus EV/EBITDA per the FMCG card. At a trailing P/E of 66.3x the stock is above the 40–65x FMCG norm, EV/EBITDA of 62.4x sits at P93 against the broad-market peer set, and the price is at 83% of its 52-week range, so it is expensive. The 42.6x forward P/E and a 90-day FY EPS upgrade of +15.5% show that strong growth is already in the price. The biggest risk is that Q2FY27 results came out today and have not been extracted yet. Management itself flagged lower margins after the summer season and packaging cost pressure from rising crude, so the Q1 margin may not hold.

fundamental.thesis: Sonata Software is a mid-cap IT company with two parts: international IT services, focused on Microsoft and Dynamics work and AI-led modernisation, and a large, low-margin domestic business that resells Microsoft and other software. The latest results we have from official filings are from Q1FY26 (June 2025), when revenue was ₹2,965 cr (+17.3% YoY) and PAT was ₹109 cr (+3.5% YoY), giving a thin 3.7% PAT margin, down from 4.2% in FY25. Underneath that, constant-currency services growth turned negative (-2.4% vs +3.9%), utilisation slipped and attrition rose to 16%, while deal wins (TCV) improved to $105M. The Q2FY27 results filed on 5 November 2026 have not been extracted yet, so this view is stale by several quarters. On price, the trailing P/E of 15.6x (forward 12.7x) and EV/EBITDA of 12.2x are well below the 22–30x IT sector range and near the bottom fifth of the broad market, so the stock grades cheap on P/E and EV/EBITDA (P/E is meaningful for this asset-light, profitable business). The biggest risk is that it is a value trap: sell-side EPS estimates have been cut about 7–8% over 90 days, and AI-driven price deflation in legacy services could keep shrinking growth and margins.

fundamental.thesis: Adani Energy Solutions is India's largest private power-transmission company, with about 30% share of recent transmission bids, 29,802 circuit km of lines, a Mumbai distribution business, a fast-growing smart-meter business and a newly consolidated energy-trading platform. In H1 FY27, revenue rose 47.5% YoY to ₹19,787 cr and PAT rose 137% to ₹2,600 cr, a 13.1% PAT margin, after Q1 FY27 grew revenue 42.4% and PAT 124%. Two caveats apply to that growth: the H1 figures restate prior periods to include the energy-trading platform, and they count ₹4,961 cr of construction revenue (SCA, up from ₹3,692 cr). The extracted H1 rows also conflict (₹14,351 cr vs ₹19,787 cr). We grade valuation on EV/EBITDA plus P/B against ROE, the yardstick for capital-intensive utilities: EV/EBITDA of 25.1x, P/B of 7.2x on a 9.7% ROE and trailing P/E of 81.7x are far above the 10–18x utilities range, and the stock sits at 89.5% of its 52-week range. Analysts raising FY EPS estimates by about 16% in 30 days and a ₹87,222 cr transmission order book give good visibility, but the price already assumes flawless delivery. The main risks are leverage and execution: debt/equity is 1.84x, net debt is ₹41,067 cr, free cash flow is negative (₹-3,185 cr in H1), capex guidance is ₹21,000–25,000 cr a year, and Adani group news can move the stock regardless of results.

fundamental.thesis: Reliance Power is a midcap private generator with about 5.3 GW operating, mostly coal (Sasan ultra-mega plant with a long-term contract, running at about 92% load factor, plus Rosa). Only 145 MW is renewable, and another 4.8 GW of renewable and hydro capacity is stuck in the pipeline. In Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 3.8% YoY to ₹1,956 cr and PAT rose 44.9% YoY to ₹65 cr, a thin 3.3% PAT margin. This follows a FY26 loss of ₹337 cr, which came after a ₹38,160 cr asset write-down. The 'accelerating' revenue signal is mostly noise across quarters: growth has gone +12.2%, ~+1.5%, +0.5%, +3.8%, so the real picture is low-single-digit growth with no management guidance. I used EV/EBITDA, the right measure for a capital-heavy power company, plus P/B. At 8.3x EV/EBITDA (P8 vs the broad market) and 0.69x book, the stock looks cheap. But ROE is negative at -2.1% and interest costs eat about 18% of revenue, so a large part of the discount is a fair price for balance-sheet and governance risk, not a clear mispricing. The biggest risk is group solvency: auditors have flagged going-concern doubts, subsidiary RSTEPL has defaulted on about ₹2,296 cr of debt, and lenders have called a parent guarantee of about ₹1,842 cr for SMPL, which is now in insolvency proceedings. Any of these could wipe out the equity value that the low P/B seems to offer.

Vardhman Textiles is one of India's largest integrated yarn and fabric makers, with an acrylic-fibre subsidiary. It is a cyclical, capital-heavy textile business rather than a true consumer-discretionary franchise. Growth has turned around sharply after a flat FY26 (revenue +0.9%, PAT -15.6%). From the H1 and Q1 filings, implied Q2FY27 revenue is about ₹2,866 cr (+15.6% YoY) and PAT is about ₹358 cr (+91% YoY). That continues Q1's +13.3% revenue and +51.5% PAT, and EBITDA margin has jumped from 13.4% in FY26 to 21.5% in H1. The quarter was cash-backed: CFO/PAT was 1.48x and H1 free cash flow was ₹468 cr. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-intensive textile business. At 15.2x it sits well below the broad-market median of 23.3x (P26), and forward P/E is 14.6x against 25.3x trailing. But P/B of 1.85x on an ROE of only 7.3%, with the stock at 98% of its 52-week range, makes it fair rather than cheap. The bull case depends on margins holding near 21%, which is very high for a textile cycle, while sell-side FY EPS estimates are down 6.5% over 90 days and a change-in-management filing landed on results day.

fundamental.thesis: Aster DM Healthcare runs hospitals and, after the merger with Quality Care India closed on 1 July 2026, is one of India's largest hospital platforms: 38 hospitals and 10,840+ beds across 27 cities under the Aster, CARE, Evercare and KIMS brands. Trailing P/E of 123x is at P97, it trades at 85% of its 52-week range, and analysts cut FY EPS estimates by 8.9% in the last 30 days. Taken together, the stock looks expensive. The biggest risk is that merger integration or a slowdown in occupancy gains falls short of the growth already priced in.

fundamental.thesis: Anupam Rasayan makes custom-synthesis specialty chemicals for agrochem, pharma and personal-care customers, and has now moved into finished medicines by buying a 50.07% controlling stake in Bliss GVS Pharma. Trailing P/E is 83.7x (P89), and P/B of 4.4x is backed by only 5.8% ROE. The forward P/E of 42x already assumes earnings roughly double. The biggest risk is that this optimism is not met: FY earnings estimates have been cut 22% over 90 days, free cash flow was negative in FY26 (Rs -221 Cr), and integrating Bliss GVS brings execution risk.

fundamental.thesis: Swiggy is India's number-two food-delivery and quick-commerce (Instamart) platform, with a small but fast-growing out-of-home dining segment. Revenue keeps growing in the mid-30s: H1 FY27 rose 36.7% to ₹14,383 cr, and the implied Q2 is about ₹7,571 cr, up roughly 36% YoY, slower than FY26's +51.4%. The trend-table label 'accelerating' mixes half-year, full-year and quarterly periods and overstates the move. Losses are narrowing on a YoY basis: the H1 EBITDA loss fell to ₹997 cr from ₹1,606 cr and H1 net loss to ₹1,713 cr from ₹2,289 cr. Sequentially, however, the Q2 loss widened to about ₹922 cr from ₹791 cr in Q1. Food delivery is close to breakeven at a -7.65% margin, but Instamart still lost ₹1,415 cr at a -55.9% margin. Because P/E and EV/EBITDA are meaningless while the company is loss-making, I graded valuation on EV/sales plus unit-economics delivery, as the sector card prescribes for platforms. Price/sales of 2.89x (about 2.3x on annualised H1 revenue) and P/B of 3.35x (P37 vs the broad market) look fair, not stretched, for ~36% growth with improving margins. Sell-side estimates have been revised sharply upward (FY EPS +50.7% over 90 days), but there is no formal management guidance, and the main risk is that the Instamart cash burn in the quick-commerce price war delays group profitability.

Indiamart runs a large Indian B2B online marketplace, with 8.9 million supplier storefronts and 217 thousand paying suppliers, and earns mainly from advance-paid supplier subscriptions, which makes it a platform rather than a typical consumer company. Comparing like quarters (the pre-computed trend signals mix quarterly and full-year figures), Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9.7% YoY to Rs 429 cr, slowing from +12% a year earlier, while PAT rose about 10% to Rs 91 cr, EBITDA margin improved from 33% to 37%, and PAT margin stayed flat near 21%; however, paying suppliers fell 2% and collections grew only 9%, so growth depends on higher revenue per supplier rather than more customers, though cash conversion is strong at 1.48x CFO/PAT. Valuation is fair using a platform yardstick of EV/EBITDA and unit economics: EV/EBITDA of 18.1x and trailing P/E of 27.1x sit below the broad-market medians of 23.3x and 35.2x (no close peers are available), and cash of Rs 3,234 cr is about 25% of market cap, but trailing P/E rests on FY26 PAT of Rs 475 cr, while annualising the latest quarter gives about 35x, and the 20.7x forward P/E assumes a profit recovery that the Rs 91 cr quarter does not yet show. The biggest risk is that a shrinking paying-supplier base eventually limits pricing power and pulls revenue growth down toward or below the current 9% collections growth; the Rs 1,939 consensus target is also not relied on because its stated +23% upside conflicts with a price of about Rs 2,137 implied by the 52-week range.

fundamental.thesis: Urban Company is India's largest online platform for home services such as beauty, cleaning and repairs, and it also sells its own water purifiers and smart locks (Native), runs international operations and has a Saudi joint venture. It is now funding a heavily loss-making quick home-help business called InstaHelp. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹537 cr, up 41% YoY, faster than FY26's +36%. Orders rose 103% and Net Transaction Value (NTV, the total value of services booked) rose 39% to ₹1,432 cr. Profit went the other way: consolidated adjusted EBITDA was -₹144 cr, a -26.8% margin, against +6.8% for FY26. That is because InstaHelp lost ₹174 cr, which wiped out a core business that is profitable and improving (core EBITDA ₹30 cr, up 213% YoY; India consumer margin 3.5%, up 110 bps). Since the business is pre-profit, P/E means nothing here, so I graded valuation on price-to-sales and unit economics instead. At 12.3x sales and 8.6x book value (76th percentile of the broad market), the price is reasonable for 40% growth only if InstaHelp's losses keep shrinking. InstaHelp's loss per order did improve 19% from the previous quarter but is still ₹279. I rate valuation fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is that the InstaHelp cash burn continues while the newly approved ₹2,500 cr capital raise dilutes shareholders, in a risk-off market that punishes high-multiple loss-makers.

Using the sector card's P/E yardstick for carmakers, cross-checked with EV/EBITDA, the stock is fair: 27.64x trailing P/E sits near the top of the 18-30x norm and matches the peer median of 27.1x (P60), and 18.32x EV/EBITDA is exactly at the peer median (P50), though my rough trailing-profit estimate of about Rs 13,150 cr implies closer to 31x, and the 20.82x forward P/E needs profit of about Rs 19,700 cr, roughly 50% higher. fundamental.thesis: Tata Steel is India's largest integrated steel producer (~35 MTPA capacity) with significant global operations in the UK (TSUK) and Netherlands (TSN), making it a spread-cycle business where EBITDA margin per tonne is the primary value driver — not PAT, which is distorted by depreciation and interest. FY26 revenue grew +6.2% YoY to ₹2,32,140 cr with PAT recovering +243% to ₹10,886 cr on a low base; Q1FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 134 bps YoY to 15.4% (the key sector KPI, and a positive signal), though PAT margin has dipped to 3.9% vs FY26's 4.7% run-rate — partly reflecting an extraordinary ₹294 cr depreciation charge with a further ₹1,178 cr expected in FY27; CFO/PAT of 2.52× confirms cash-backed earnings quality. Using EV/EBITDA as the appropriate yardstick for capital-intensive steel, TATASTEEL trades at 10.45× — above the sector card's mid-cycle steel benchmark of 5–8× but at a 41.6% discount to the 16-stock materials sector median of 17.9× (P13, with the median inflated by paint companies); a forward P/E of 10.78× vs trailing 23.46× implies substantial earnings recovery is priced in, supporting a fair grade rather than cheap given above-mid-cycle positioning. The primary risk is Tata Steel Netherlands (TSN), where the Dutch Environmental Agency has signaled intent to revoke operating permits for its Coke & Gas Plants, with going-concern material uncertainty formally disclosed — an unresolved regulatory outcome that could trigger material asset impairment and structurally reduce consolidated earnings capacity.

Info Edge runs Naukri, India's leading online jobs platform, along with 99acres, Jeevansathi and Shiksha, and recruitment remains its main profit engine with a 58.7% H1 operating margin, up 448 bps. H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 1,760 cr (+10.2% YoY) and PAT was Rs 1,140 cr (+65.1%), but subtracting Q1 implies a more ordinary Q2 of about Rs 891 cr revenue (about +10.5%) and Rs 384 cr PAT (about +11%, about 43% margin), so the 'expanding' margin signal looks distorted by Q1's unusually high 87% margin, likely including non-operating gains, and by FY26 figures that appear understated about 10x; recruitment billings also slowed from about 17% in Q1 (implied) to 12.6% in Q2, though management cites timing effects and puts underlying growth at 14-15%, while 99acres billings accelerated to +21.2%. Using EV/EBITDA and growth delivery as the platform yardstick, I grade valuation fair: EV/EBITDA of 53.0x is 10% above the peer median (P78), while the 44.7x trailing P/E (P22) may be flattered by non-operating income and the 1.33x P/B (P0) looks less meaningful with ROE at just 4.6%; the stock sits near its 52-week low, but the price basis needs checking because the 14.4% range position implies about Rs 1,000 while the consensus upside implies about Rs 1,180, and the 146% dividend yield is clearly bad data. The biggest risk is that recruitment billings stay near or below the 12.6% Q2 pace rather than returning to management's 14-15% underlying estimate, which would undermine the multiple in a risk-off market where crude and sector positioning are also headwinds.

fundamental.thesis: Sagility is a mid-cap healthcare outsourcing company. About 90% of revenue comes from US health insurers (payers) and about 10% from hospitals and other providers. It is tagged IT here, but its demand comes from US healthcare operations, not tech spending. In Q2FY27 revenue was ₹2,032 cr, up 22.5% YoY, and PAT was ₹284 cr, up 13.3%. Growth has slowed from +35.7% (Q3FY26) to +29.1% (FY26) to +25.0% (H1) to +22.5%, and constant-currency growth is only about 12%, so roughly half the headline growth comes from the weak rupee. Reported PAT margin fell to 14.0% from 15.1% a year ago, and adjusted PAT grew only 8.1% even though adjusted EBITDA margin reached a six-quarter high of 26.3%. On valuation, using P/E and EV/EBITDA, the trailing P/E of 21.5x is below the IT sector's 22–30x range and sits at about the 24th percentile of the broad market (there are no close peers in the universe). EV/EBITDA is 11.4x, forward P/E is 15.4x, and cash conversion is strong (CFO/PAT 1.27x), so the stock looks cheap. The biggest risk is client concentration: the top 3 clients are 60% of revenue and the top 10 are 84%, and voluntary attrition is high at 25.7%. Losing or repricing a single large client could hurt badly. The yfinance dividend yield (44%) and debt/equity (11.5) figures look like unit errors, so I ignored them.

For a capital-intensive manufacturer we used EV/EBITDA rather than P/E: at 32.7x it sits at P69 of the broad market, and the forward P/E of 41.9x is at P85. The trailing P/E of 159x is P99 at an ROE of only 5.6%. On every yardstick the stock is expensive, and the price already assumes a strong earnings recovery. E.I.D. Parry is mainly a farm-inputs group: nutrients and crop protection through its subsidiary CIL made up about 90% of Q1 FY27 segment revenue, with sugar, distillery, nutraceuticals and consumer products much smaller, so the FMCG tag and P/E norms fit poorly. Revenue growth has slowed from +29.3% in Q1 FY26 to +18.3% in Q3 FY26 and +3.4% (Rs 9,018 cr) in Q1 FY27, with the NACL acquisition's boost lapsing from August 2026, while PAT fell 42.5% to Rs 142 cr, EBITDA margin slipped from 10.3% to 8.7%, sugar revenue fell 62% after the refinery closure, and distillery revenue fell 13.5%. Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick, with P/B as a cross-check, the stock looks cheap at 5.96x (P2 of the broad market, with no tight peers) and 1.53x book, despite a less clear 29.06x trailing P/E, but consolidated multiples include profit owed to minority holders, some discount looks earned, and the 10.1x forward P/E rests on one analyst whose estimates were cut about 30% in 90 days. The biggest risk is that low price masks weak earnings quality, as FY26 CFO/PAT was only 0.02x, FCF was Rs -64 cr, and the Q2 FY27 results due on 13 Nov could bring further cuts; some extracted figures also look unreliable, including the Rs 61,000 cr refinery investment, the 23.65 debt/equity reading (possibly 23.65%, or about 0.24x) and the +67.6% target upside (about +39% at the implied price near Rs 756).
